native: full-width blue capsule action bar is an iOS idiom

native: centred rule-flanked section headers, mixed capitalization
native: same tells as shot-2 (OS variant of same surface)
native: centred floating modal, not a top-anchored native sheet
native: ~26pt iOS-style filled-blue rounded checkboxes (kit macOS checkbox is 14pt)
correct hierarchy here: Start primary + Back as plain text

buttons/links/active/focus; reads bound to system blue (kit dark #0091FF)
LARGER than 13pt macOS body — iOS-density tell

tokens.value: ~14pt secondary grey, centred between hairline rules
full content-width x ~45pt capsule, circle-badged glyph
tokens.notes: iOS bottom-CTA transplant; kit XL control = 36pt
genuine native pop-up button — pro-native tell

patterns.key_values: linear fixed-portrait wizard; centred rule-flanked section labels; persistent bottom action bar with one full-width blue capsule primary + a Back/secondary as plain text below it
step/stage progress list — full-width cards; completed=green check, active=navy-tinted card w/ determinate bar + % + speed/size counters, pending=dimmed glyph
config form: grey info/requirement cards w/ glyph + bullet list; [field | bordered | bordered | filled-blue] button row; native pop-up drive selector; tinted status + warning cards
centred floating modal (NOT a native sheet) over dimmed content; ~26pt blue checkboxes incl. a correctly-dimmed disabled one; trailing blue capsule Done
welcome screen (cover): centred USB icon + wordmark + tagline + single blue Start capsule + support footer

signature_moves: Persistent full-width blue capsule action bar with a circle-badged directional glyph (Continue/Start/Cancel/Stop) — iOS bottom-CTA transplanted to a Mac window; the app's whole identity, unmissable next-step, but a non-native idiom

Tinted status-card semantics (navy=in-progress, green=success, amber=destructive-warning), each ALWAYS paired with a glyph + text label — colour is never the sole signal (the app's real accessibility strength)
defects: Focal Collision — two saturated-blue filled primaries in one view (Analyze + Continue, shot-2/3)
Inconsistent abort styling — loud full-width blue Cancel (shot-1) vs quiet dark-ghost Stop (shot-6) for the same action class
Focal weight on the wrong control — Cancel (an abort) is the single loudest element in shot-1; abort/destructive should never be the prominent default
Non-native section headers — centred labels flanked by hairline rules, mixed capitalization ('File selection' vs 'USB Drive Selection')
Non-native modality — centred floating modal instead of a top-anchored native sheet (shot-4)
iOS-density controls (tell) — ~45pt buttons, ~26pt checkboxes, ~34pt pop-ups, ~15px body on a pointer-first platform

aesthetic.direction: dark-neutral product surface (near-black ground, tonal grey cards, one electric-blue accent) pushed toward consumer utility by iOS-sized oversized controls and full-width pill CTAs — neo-grotesque-product body language with a Setup-Assistant wizard spine
peers: Apple Setup Assistant / macOS Installer wizard

psychology: Goal-Gradient / Zeigarnik — step lists with green checks + an active card showing %, speed and byte counters give earned, motivating progress feedback toward completion
Von Restorff — the single full-width blue button is the one different thing, pulling the eye to the next action (misused in shot-1 where the different thing is Cancel/abort)
Fitts's Law — window-width capsule buttons are huge easy targets (arguably over-applied for a pointer platform)
Hick's Law — choices reduced to one obvious action per step (violated in the config view's dual primaries)
Forgiveness (Lidwell) — proportional amber WARNING before an irreversible drive erase; weakened by styling Continue identically loud regardless of the destructive consequence
Jakob's Law — linear installer wizard matches users' trained mental model of bootable-media tools
Doherty Threshold — continuous MB/s + %/byte counters keep the long write feeling responsive
notes: Task was Workflow A (UI) only — icon and cover analysed as brand context, no icons/ file written. Lineage is the key judgement call: macOS-correct chrome (real traffic lights, disabled-grey zoom on a fixed portrait window, a genuine double-chevron pop-up button) argues native SwiftUI, but the body is styled in an iOS-consumer idiom (oversized full-width buttons, ~26pt filled-blue checkboxes, centred floating modal, ~15px body). Classified native/med so its taste is admissible in principle, but every iOS-idiom token is flagged as a tell/defect and must NOT feed macOS canon. Rated ~12.7/14 cross-platform (it is internally systematic and accessible) but only ~5.2/10 native-tells (it does not read as a native Mac app). Colours estimated from compressed @2x dark-mode PNGs — wide ranges. shot-2/shot-3 are the same surface (macOS vs Windows source variants).
